title: Two Clocks, One Timeline: Putting Streams That Do Not Tick Together on the Same Instants

questions.question: A 10 Hz stream is used at a 100 Hz loop by taking the newest value it has sent. How old can that value be?
options: Up to a whole sample, and half a sample on average
questions.explanation: 0.2384 rms error on a 1 Hz sine. A held value is as old as the gap since its sample.

questions.question: How is a stream read at an instant between two samples?
options: Join the sample before and the sample after with a line and read it at the instant
questions.explanation: Interpolation, by binary search for the two samples.

questions.question: A sine at 1 Hz is sampled at 10 Hz. How do the two methods compare?
options: The line is about ten times closer
questions.explanation: Rms error 0.0253 against 0.2384 held, matching the 0.0255 and 0.2565 the maths gives. Held error goes with the frequency, a line's with its square.

questions.question: What should interpolation do before the first sample or after the last?
options: Say no and leave the output untouched
questions.explanation: There is nothing to join. A made up value is worse than none.

questions.question: A stream has a hole from 1.0 s to 1.6 s and a max_gap of 0.15 s. What happens to an instant at 1.3 s?
options: It is interpolated across the hole
questions.explanation: 192 of 251 instants were and none of the 59 in the hole. A line across a gap is a guess about time the sensor never saw.

questions.question: What does interpolation cost that holding does not?
options: It needs a sample after the instant
questions.explanation: It answers for a moment one sample in the past. That is the price of the better answer.
